intro: OneTrust is a consent management platform configured through a web-based admin console. Changes take effect when you republish the script — no developer deployment is usually required for category-level fixes, though blocking third-party tags requires a change to your tag manager or site code.

sections.title: Audit which cookies are assigned to which category
steps: Log in to your OneTrust account at app.onetrust.com.
Navigate to Websites → Categorisation (or Cookie Compliance → Cookies).
Search for each cookie named in the CRITICAL findings. Verify it is assigned to the correct category (e.g. Analytics, Targeting). If it is uncategorised, assign it now.
For cookies set by third-party vendors (Google Analytics, Meta, etc.), check whether the vendor's script is blocked until the corresponding category is accepted.

sections.title: Ensure scripts are blocked before consent
steps: In OneTrust, go to Websites → Scripts. Each script entry should be mapped to a cookie category.
Enable 'Script Blocking' for all non-essential vendor scripts. OneTrust wraps the script tags so they fire only after consent.

Alternatively, if tags are managed via Google Tag Manager: add an OneTrust Consent Mode variable and use it as a trigger condition on each tag. Tags must NOT fire when the consent state is unknown or denied.
Deploy the updated script (republish in OneTrust and verify the new version loads on your site).

sections.title: Add a 'Reject All' button to the first-layer banner
steps: In OneTrust, go to Preference Center → Banner.
Under Button Configuration, add a second primary button. Label it 'Reject all' and set its action to 'Reject All'.
Ensure the button has equal visual weight to 'Accept all' — same size, same contrast, same layer. Do not hide it inside a 'More options' link.
Republish and test: visiting the site in a fresh private window should show both 'Accept all' and 'Reject all' on the first visible banner.

sections.title: Verify the fix with a re-scan
steps: After republishing, run the cookie scanner again against the same URL.
Confirm: no-interaction scenario sets zero non-essential cookies.
Confirm: reject-all scenario shows only strictly-necessary cookies.
Confirm: both accept-all and reject-all complete in a single click from the first-layer banner.
